questions.q: Prokinetics increase movement/contraction of the GIT in which direction?
opts: They do not alter contraction direction
questions.exp: Drugs that ↑ movement/contraction of GIT in the cranio-caudal direction (Book p266)

questions.q: The classic use of prokinetics is ____.
questions.exp: Use: gastroparesis (Book p266)

questions.q: Match the prokinetic strategy to its target.
right: (-) CCK → removes its brake on contraction
questions.exp: Erythromycin/mitemcinal (+) motilin; dexloxiglumide (-) CCK; 5HT4 agonists (+) → ↑ACh; D2 blockers remove dopamine inhibition → ↑ACh (Book p266)

questions.q: 5-HT and D2 receptors are called ____ in the GIT because they alter acetylcholine (ACh) levels.
questions.exp: 5HT & D2 receptors are heteroreceptors in GIT as they alter ACh levels (Book p266)

questions.q: The macrolide that acts as a prokinetic via (+) motilin is ____.
questions.exp: Erythromycin (and mitemcinal) → (+) motilin (Book p266)

questions.q: Dexloxiglumide promotes motility by ____ CCK.
questions.exp: Dexloxiglumide (-) CCK (Book p266)

questions.q: The 5-HT4 agonists banned due to QT prolongation are:
questions.exp: Cisapride, tegaserod — banned (D/t S/E: QT prolongation) (Book p266)

questions.q: Mosapride and prucalopride are used for:
questions.exp: Mosapride, prucalopride — use: GERD, chronic constipation (Book p266)

questions.q: The side effect of 5-HT4 agonists is ____.
questions.exp: S/E: diarrhoea (Book p266)

questions.q: Metoclopramide at normal dose blocks D2; at high dose it additionally:
questions.exp: Normal dose (−)D2; high dose (+)5-HT4, (−)D2, (−)5-HT3 (Book p266)

questions.q: Which receptor action pair of metoclopramide gives prokinetic PLUS antiemetic effect?
questions.exp: (−)D2 + (−)5-HT3 → prokinetic + antiemetic; (−)D2 + (+)5-HT4 → prokinetic (Book p266)

questions.q: Domperidone's MOA is ____ only.
questions.exp: Domperidone: (−)D2 → prokinetic + antiemetic (Book p266)

questions.q: Domperidone's potency is ____ than metoclopramide's.
questions.exp: Domperidone potency < than metoclopramide (Book p266)

questions.q: Metoclopramide's uses include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Mild–moderate antiemetic case is domperidone's slot; metoclopramide: CINV, gastroparesis, paralytic ileus, hiccups, bowel cleansing (Book p266)

questions.q: The earliest EPS symptom of metoclopramide is ____.
questions.exp: EPS: acute dystonia (earliest symptom) (Book p266)

questions.q: Regarding BBB crossing:
opts: Metoclopramide crosses in major concentration (EPS); domperidone in minor concentration (minor EPS)
Domperidone crosses in major concentration; metoclopramide does not cross
Both cross equally with equal EPS
questions.exp: Metoclopramide: major conc. crosses BBB → EPS; domperidone: minor conc. → minor EPS (Book p266)

questions.q: Hyperprolactinemia is severe with metoclopramide but mild with domperidone, which is therefore used for ____ stimulation.
questions.exp: Domperidone: mild hyperprolactinemia — used for prolactin stimulation (Book p266)

questions.q: The shortest acting 5-HT3 antagonist (IM/oral) is ____.
questions.exp: Ondansetron: shortest acting (IM/oral) (Book p267)

questions.q: The longest acting and most potent 5-HT3 antagonist is ____.
questions.exp: Palonosetron: longest acting + most potent (Book p267)

questions.q: Early-onset chemotherapy induced nausea & vomiting: DOC is ____.
questions.exp: Early onset: ondansetron (DOC) (Book p267)

questions.q: Late-onset chemotherapy induced nausea & vomiting is covered by ____.
questions.exp: Late onset: palonosetron (Book p267)

questions.q: Post-operative & post-radiotherapy nausea & vomiting: DOC class is ____.
questions.exp: Post operative & post radiotherapy nausea & vomiting (DOC) — 5HT3 antagonists (Book p267)

questions.q: The third listed use of 5-HT3 antagonists is ____.
questions.exp: 3. Morning sickness (Book p267)

questions.q: QT prolongation with 5-HT3 antagonists is maximum with ____.
questions.exp: QT prolongation: max dolasetron (Book p267)

questions.q: QT prolongation with 5-HT3 antagonists is minimum with ____.
questions.exp: QT prolongation: min palonosetron (Book p267)

questions.q: 5-HT3 antagonists are C/I in ____ induced nausea & vomiting because of ↑ risk of hypotension.
questions.exp: C/I: apomorphine induced nausea & vomiting → ↑ risk of hypotension (Book p267)

questions.q: Late-onset nausea & vomiting: DOC class is ____ inhibitors.
questions.exp: Late onset nausea vomiting: DOC — neurokinin-1 inhibitors (Book p267)

questions.q: The NK1 inhibitor given only I/V is ____.
questions.exp: Fosaprepitant (IV); aprepitant (oral/IV) (Book p267)

questions.q: The NK1 inhibitor also used for severe cough is ____.
questions.exp: Severe cough: aprepitant (Book p267)

questions.q: The cannabinoid receptor agonists are dronabinol and ____.
questions.exp: Drugs: dronabinol, nabilone (Book p267)

questions.q: The cannabinoid receptor (CBR) carries which inhibitory subunit?
questions.exp: Cannabinoid receptor (inhibitory subunit) — Gi (Book p267)

questions.q: Cannabinoids ↓ release of 5HT, dopamine and NE, reducing effect on 5HT3 and D2 receptors but having NO effect on:
questions.exp: ↓ effect on 5HT3 & D2 receptors but no effect on α1 receptors → antiemetic effect (Book p267)

questions.q: Cannabinoid side effects: hypotension (monitor BP) and ____.
questions.exp: S/E: hypotension — monitor BP; blood shot eyes (Book p267)

questions.q: Match the antiemetic drug to its book use.
right: Chemotherapy induced nausea/vomiting; transdermal patch 4.5 hrs before travel
questions.exp: Levosulpiride → post-op N/V, gastroparesis; olanzapine → CINV, transdermal patch 4.5 hrs before travel; scopolamine → DOC motion sickness; doxylamine → DOC morning sickness (Book p268)

questions.q: The antihistamines listed for motion sickness are:
questions.exp: Antihistamines: diphenhydramine, dimenhydrinate, promethazine, cyclizine (meclizine) — motion sickness (Book p268)

questions.q: The antihistamine that is DOC for morning sickness is ____.
questions.exp: Doxylamine: DOC for morning sickness (Book p268)

questions.q: The anticholinergic that is DOC for motion sickness is ____.
questions.exp: Scopolamine: DOC for motion sickness (Book p268)

questions.q: ____ is an add-on for chemotherapy induced nausea & vomiting.
questions.exp: Dexamethasone: add on for chemotherapy induced nausea & vomiting (Book p268)

units.title: Prokinetics: Definition, Pathways and 5-HT4 Agonists
units.sec: Prokinetics: Definition, Pathways and 5-HT4 Agonists · p266
units.guide: ↑ GIT movement cranio-caudal; use gastroparesis. Erythromycin/mitemcinal (+) motilin; dexloxiglumide (−) CCK; 5-HT4 agonists ↑ACh; D2 blockers remove dopamine brake. 5HT & D2 = heteroreceptors. Cisapride/tegaserod banned (QT); mosapride/prucalopride → GERD, chronic constipation; S/E diarrhoea.

units.title: D2 Blockers: Metoclopramide vs Domperidone
units.sec: D2 Blockers: Metoclopramide vs Domperidone · p266
units.guide: Metoclopramide: normal dose (−)D2; high dose adds (+)5-HT4, (−)5-HT3. (−)D2+(−)5-HT3 → prokinetic+antiemetic. Domperidone (−)D2 only, less potent, minor BBB. EPS earliest = acute dystonia (metoclopramide). Hyperprolactinemia severe (metoclopramide) vs mild — domperidone used for prolactin stimulation.

units.title: 5-HT3 Antagonists
units.guide: All oral. Ondansetron shortest (early CINV DOC); palonosetron longest + most potent (late CINV, min QT); dolasetron max QT. DOC post-op/post-radiotherapy N/V; morning sickness. S/E constipation/diarrhea, headache, QT, hypotension. C/I apomorphine-induced N/V.

units.title: Neurokinin-1 Inhibitors
units.guide: Aprepitant (oral/IV), fosaprepitant (IV), netupitant, rolapitant. Late-onset N/V: DOC. Severe cough: aprepitant.

units.title: Cannabinoid Receptor Agonists
units.guide: Dronabinol, nabilone stimulate CBR (Gi) → ↓ release of 5HT/Dop/NE → ↓ effect on 5HT3 & D2 but no effect on α1 → antiemetic. S/E: hypotension (monitor BP), blood shot eyes.

units.title: Other Antiemetics and Dexamethasone
units.guide: Levosulpiride: post-op N/V, gastroparesis. Olanzapine: CINV, transdermal patch 4.5 hrs before travel. Scopolamine: DOC motion sickness. Doxylamine: DOC morning sickness. Antihistamines (diphenhydramine, dimenhydrinate, promethazine, cyclizine/meclizine): motion sickness. Dexamethasone: add-on CINV.
